examples.en: I was upset because my friend coldly hung up on me.

examples.ko: 그렇게 매정한 말을 들으니 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Hearing such cold words made me cry.

examples.ko: 동생은 겉으로는 매정해 보이지만 속은 따뜻해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling looks cold on the outside but is warm inside.
How can you be so heartless?
The boss who used to be cold smiled at me today.
That person has become cold, and he feels like a stranger.

explain: '차갑다'는 온도나 분위기에도 쓰지만, '매정하다'는 정을 줘야 할 때 정 없이 대하는 사람에게만 써요. 보통 '매정하게 끊다', '매정하게 거절하다'처럼 행동 앞에 붙어요. 반대말은 '다정하다'예요.
explain_en: 차갑다 can describe temperature or mood, but 매정하다 is only used for a person who acts without warmth when warmth is expected. It usually comes before an action, as in '매정하게 거절하다' (to refuse coldly). The opposite is 다정하다.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 제가 세상에서 제일 못난이 같았어요.
examples.en: As a child, I felt like the plainest person in the world.
I bought oddly shaped potatoes cheaply at the market.

examples.ko: 할머니는 막내 손자를 우리 못난이라고 불러요.
examples.en: Grandmother calls her youngest grandson her little goof.
I was embarrassed that I cried like a fool in front of people.
The misfits got together and comforted each other.

examples.ko: 저는 못난이가 아니라고 친구가 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend told me I am not a loser.

explain: '못생기다'는 얼굴 모양만 말하지만 '못난이'는 하는 짓이 모자란 사람에게도 써요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 기분이 상할 수 있어서, 가족끼리 귀엽게 부르거나 '못난이 감자'처럼 모양이 고르지 않은 채소와 과일에 편하게 써요.
explain_en: 못생기다 is only about looks, but 못난이 can also refer to someone who acts foolishly. Said directly to a person it can hurt, so people use it affectionately within a family, or for vegetables and fruit with uneven shapes, as in '못난이 감자'.

examples.en: My stomach hurts often, so I booked an appointment at the gynecology department.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 부인과와 내과가 같이 있어요.
examples.en: This hospital has both gynecology and internal medicine.
Which floor is the gynecology department on?
My older sister went to get a gynecological checkup.

examples.ko: 부인과 의사 선생님이 친절하게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The gynecologist explained everything kindly.

examples.ko: 부인과 쪽 병원은 아침부터 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Gynecology clinics are crowded from the morning.

explain: 보통은 '산부인과'라고 말하고, '부인과'만 따로 쓰는 일은 적어서 병원 안내판이나 진료과 이름에서 볼 수 있어요. 임신과 출산은 '산과', 여성 몸의 질환은 '부인과'로 나눠요.
explain_en: People usually say 산부인과, and 부인과 alone mostly appears on hospital signs and department names. 산과 covers pregnancy and childbirth, while 부인과 covers women's health conditions.

examples.en: How much is the meeting room fee per hour?

examples.ko: 이 앱은 사용료를 내야 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pay a fee to use this app.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 사용료가 싸지만 위치가 불편해요.
examples.en: The fee for this building is cheap, but the location is inconvenient.
You also have to pay the campsite fee in advance.
You only need to pay the usage fee every month.
They maintain the facility with the fees they receive.

explain: '사용료'는 쓴 만큼 내는 돈이고 '이용료'도 거의 같은 상황에 써요. 방이나 땅을 빌릴 때는 '임대료', 물건을 빌릴 때는 '대여료'라고 해요. '사용료를 내다', '사용료를 받다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: 사용료 is money paid for what you use, and 이용료 fits almost the same situations. Renting a room or land is 임대료, and renting an item is 대여료. It pairs with '사용료를 내다' (to pay) and '사용료를 받다' (to charge).

examples.en: Morning sickness makes every morning hard for me.

examples.ko: 언니는 입덧이 심해서 음식을 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: My sister has severe morning sickness and can hardly eat.

examples.ko: 친구는 입덧을 할 때 귤만 먹었대요.
examples.en: My friend says she only ate tangerines when she had morning sickness.

examples.ko: 입덧에 좋은 음식이 있으면 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If there is food that helps with morning sickness, please tell me.

examples.ko: 임신 초기에는 입덧으로 고생하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people suffer from morning sickness in early pregnancy.
Morning sickness differs from person to person, so don't worry.

explain: '입덧을 하다', '입덧이 심하다'처럼 써요. 속이 울렁거리는 일반 증상은 '멀미'나 '메스꺼움'이라고 하고, 입덧은 임신했을 때만 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '입덧을 하다' or '입덧이 심하다'. A general queasy feeling is 멀미 or 메스꺼움, while 입덧 is only for pregnancy.

examples.en: I bought batteries at the neighborhood general store.
The general store has everything.
My grandfather runs a small general store.
The owner of the general store showed me the way.
The general store in front of the school closed down.

examples.ko: 잡화점으로 가는 길에 비가 오기 시작했어요.
examples.en: It started to rain on my way to the general store.

explain: 큰 마트나 다이소 같은 '생활용품점'과 비슷하지만, 잡화점은 동네의 작고 오래된 가게 느낌이 있어요. 요즘은 '문구점', '편의점'처럼 파는 물건에 따라 가게 이름을 더 많이 불러요.
explain_en: It is close to a '생활용품점' (household goods store) like a big mart or Daiso, but 잡화점 suggests a small, old neighborhood shop. Today people more often name shops by what they sell, such as 문구점 or 편의점.

examples.ko: 이 병은 전염성이 강해서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: This disease is highly contagious, so you need to be careful.
Colds are contagious too, so please wear a mask.

examples.ko: 전염성 높은 병에 걸리면 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: If you catch a highly contagious illness, you must rest at home.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 전염성을 확인하려고 검사를 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor ran a test to check whether it was contagious.

examples.ko: 전염성에 대한 뉴스를 보고 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: I watched the news about contagiousness and got worried.

examples.ko: 그 병은 전염성도 약하고 증상도 가벼워요.
examples.en: That illness is weakly contagious and the symptoms are mild.

explain: '전염성이 강하다', '전염성이 높다', '전염성이 약하다'처럼 써요. 감기처럼 흔한 병은 '옮다'를 더 많이 써서 '감기가 옮았어요'라고 해요. 하품이나 기분이 퍼질 때도 '전염되다'를 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '전염성이 강하다' (very contagious), '높다', or '약하다'. For common illnesses like colds, people usually say '옮다', as in '감기가 옮았어요'. '전염되다' can also describe yawns or moods spreading.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 반찬으로 무 절임이 나와요.
examples.en: This restaurant serves pickled radish as a side dish.
Pickled cucumbers are sour and crunchy.

examples.ko: 절임 음식은 너무 짜지 않게 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Pickled food should be eaten in a way that isn't too salty.

examples.ko: 할머니가 직접 만든 절임을 선물로 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother gave me pickles she made herself as a gift.
There is some pickled garlic left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 절임에 쓰는 소금은 따로 사야 해요.
examples.en: You have to buy the salt used for pickling separately.

explain: '무 절임', '오이 절임'처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 써요. 간장이나 된장에 담근 반찬은 '장아찌'라고 따로 불러요. 동사는 '절이다'이고, 김치도 배추를 절여서 만들지만 보통 절임이라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: Put the ingredient first, as in '무 절임' (pickled radish) or '오이 절임'. Side dishes preserved in soy sauce or soybean paste have their own name, 장아찌. The verb is 절이다, and although kimchi is made by salting cabbage, it is not usually called 절임.

examples.en: My friend's grandmother is coming this afternoon.
I have to write my grandmother's name on the form.

examples.ko: 조모와 함께 살았던 집이 아직 있어요.
examples.en: The house where I lived with my grandmother still exists.
I am going to see my grandmother this weekend.

examples.ko: 조모는 어릴 때 이야기를 자주 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother often told me stories from her childhood.
My grandmother will also attend the wedding.

explain: 평소에는 '할머니'라고 하고, 조모는 서류나 격식 있는 글에서 써요. 남의 할머니는 '조모님'이라고 높여요. 엄마 쪽 할머니는 '외조모'라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say 할머니, and 조모 appears in documents and formal writing. Someone else's grandmother is the honorific '조모님'. A mother's mother is '외조모'.

examples.en: I failed the exam again and felt crushed.
I overcame the frustration and started again.

examples.ko: 큰 좌절감 때문에 며칠 동안 아무것도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because of the deep discouragement, I could not do anything for several days.

examples.ko: 아무리 노력해도 안 될 때 좌절감에 빠져요.
examples.en: When nothing works no matter how hard I try, I fall into despair.

examples.ko: 좌절감은 누구나 한 번쯤 느끼는 감정이에요.
examples.en: Everyone feels this kind of frustration at least once.
Even frustration fades little by little as time passes.

explain: '좌절감을 느끼다', '좌절감에 빠지다', '좌절감을 극복하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요. '실망감'은 기대와 달라서 속상한 기분이고, 좌절감은 하려던 일이 막힌 느낌이라 더 무거워요. '절망감'은 희망이 없다고 느낄 때 써요.
explain_en: It comes with fixed partners such as '좌절감을 느끼다' (feel), '좌절감에 빠지다' (fall into), and '좌절감을 극복하다' (overcome). 실망감 is being let down because things differ from expectations, while 좌절감 is the heavier feeling of being blocked. 절망감 is used when you feel there is no hope.

en: tactlessness; lack of discretion; acting out of place (esp. for one's age)

examples.en: Please don't tease me for acting silly at my age.
Dad embarrassed me again by acting out of line.
Crying all of a sudden, I am being silly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 주책없이 큰 소리로 노래를 부르셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang loudly without any sense of occasion.

examples.ko: 회식에서 주책 부리는 상사 때문에 민망했어요.
examples.en: I felt awkward because my boss was acting inappropriately at the company dinner.
Everyone laughed because of the silly behavior.

explain: 상황이나 나이에 맞지 않게 말하고 행동하는 모습을 가볍게 놀리거나 흉볼 때 써요. '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', '주책 부리다'처럼 쓰고, '주책없다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used to lightly tease or criticize someone who talks or acts in a way that does not fit the situation or their age. It appears as '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', and '주책 부리다', and '주책없다' is very often used with almost the same meaning.

examples.en: It rained and the playground turned into mud.
The children played happily in the mud.
My shoes got dirty from walking on the muddy road.
The car is stuck in the mud and won't move.
I took a detour to avoid the mud.
I was surprised to see the road turned to mud.

explain: '진흙'은 흙 자체이고, '진흙탕'은 진흙이 가득한 길이나 웅덩이까지 넓게 가리켜요. '흙탕물'은 흙이 섞여 흐려진 물이에요. '진흙탕에 빠지다', '진흙탕이 되다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 두 회사의 가격 경쟁이 진흙탕 싸움이 됐어요.
phrases.en: The price competition between the two companies became a dirty fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 나쁜 방법까지 써서 지저분하게 다투는 모습을 비유해요. 보통 '진흙탕 싸움'이라는 덩어리로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for a messy fight where both sides use dirty tactics. It is usually used as the fixed phrase.

explain_en: 진흙 is the mud itself, while 진흙탕 also covers a road or pit full of mud. 흙탕물 is water clouded by soil. It is often used as '진흙탕에 빠지다' and '진흙탕이 되다'.

examples.en: The children are spinning tops in the yard.
This top spins for a long time, which is amazing.

examples.ko: 팽이가 쓰러지기 전에 한 번 더 쳐요.
examples.en: I hit the top once more before it falls over.

examples.ko: 시장에서 색깔이 예쁜 팽이 하나를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a top with pretty colors at the market.
I spun around like a top and sat down because I felt dizzy.

examples.ko: 얼음 위에서 팽이를 치는 놀이가 재미있어요.
examples.en: Playing with tops on the ice is fun.

explain: 줄을 감아 던져 돌리는 팽이는 '돌리다', 채로 쳐서 오래 돌게 하는 팽이는 '치다'를 같이 써요. 겨울에 얼음 위에서 하는 '팽이치기'는 한국 전통 놀이예요. '팽이버섯'의 이름에도 들어가요.
explain_en: A top you wind with a string and throw goes with '돌리다', and a top you keep spinning by hitting it with a stick goes with '치다'. '팽이치기' on winter ice is a traditional Korean game. The word is also part of '팽이버섯' (enoki mushroom).

examples.en: My successor starts work next week.
The team leader has not found a replacement yet.
I taught my successor the job step by step.
I heard the successor is someone with a lot of experience.

examples.ko: 퇴사하기 전에 후임자와 함께 일을 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before leaving the company, I sorted out the work together with my successor.

examples.ko: 후임자로 뽑힌 사람은 저와 같은 학교 출신이에요.
examples.en: The person chosen as my successor graduated from the same school as me.

explain: 회사에서 내 일을 이어받는 사람은 '후임자', 앞서 맡았던 사람은 '전임자'예요. 보통 '후임자를 구하다', '후임자로 정해지다'처럼 써요. 군대에서는 나보다 늦게 들어온 사람을 줄여서 '후임'이라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: The person who takes over your work is the 후임자, and the one who held the post before is the 전임자. It is used as '후임자를 구하다' (find a successor) or '후임자로 정해지다' (be chosen as successor). In the military, someone who joined after you is often called simply '후임'.
